Definition: nominative plural of G1473; we (only used when emphatic):--us, we (ourselves).
BiblicalUsage: Hemeis is we, the emphatic we, used when the speakers put themselves forward. In Matthew 19:27 Peter says, behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee, in Mark 10:28 he says the same, and in 1 John 3:14 John writes, we know that we have passed from death unto life.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the we is the confession of the whole church: we forsook all, and we know we have passed from death to life, because we love the brethren.
